newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Early Taiwan dollar rises on interest rate hikes.
newsitem.headline: Early Taiwan dollar rises on interest rate hikes.

text.p: The Taiwan dollar rebounded against the U.S. dollar from recent slides in early Friday trade after the central bank on Thursday decided to raise two key interest rates, dealers said.
After 15 minutes at 0115 GMT, the local unit, which had faced intense selling pressure this week, rose to T$28.590 against Thursday's sharply depreciated T$28.70 finish.
Thursday's close was the Taiwan dollar's lowest close since 1988.
Turnover through dealers on Friday was US$25 million.

The central bank on Thursday announced a modest tightening of monetary policy by raising the rediscount rate to 5.25 percent from 5.00 and accommodations against secured loans to 5.625 percent from 5.375, effective from Friday.
Central bank governor Sheu Yuan-dong said the rate hikes were intended to maintain forex market stability.
Dealers said the central bank's unexpected moves prompted some offshore speculators to take profits on the U.S. dollar.
"Offshore speculators are eager the sell U.S. dollars after the central bank's move," said one dealer at a foreign bank.
Sheu, after the central bank's quarterly board meeting, made clear the central bank was determined to clamp down speculative attacks that have shocked several southeast Asian currencies in July.
"If there are abnormal factors intervening in the market, the central bank will adopt appropriate measures to maintain the foreign exchange market's stability," he said.
Sheu would not say what he meant by "appropriate measures".
But dealers said the Taiwan dollar's gain would be limited as local importers likely would buy U.S. dollars later in the session.

"This week's Taiwan dollar depreciation came too fast too soon, many importers were not quick enough to cover their short positions. Today will be a good chance for them to hunt bargains." the dealer said.
A range of T$27.55-80 was seen for Friday.
